description_full: Futu Holdings Limited engages in the provision of digitalized securities brokerage and wealth management product distribution service in Hong Kong and internationally. It offers online financial services, including securities and derivative trades brokerage, margin financing and fund distribution services through its Futubull and Moomoo digital platforms. The company also provides financial information and online community services; online wealth management services under the Money Plus brand name through its Futubull and moomoo platforms, which provides its client access to mutual funds, private funds, bonds, structured products, and other wealth management products; market data and information services; and NiuNiu Community, an open forum for users and clients to share insights, ask questions, and exchange ideas. Futu Holdings Limited was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Admiralty, Hong Kong.

financial_summary: Futu Holdings Limited is a large-cap financial services business with a $13.4B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +44% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +7.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 27% against a 10% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $5.2B in free cash flow — roughly 178 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.60× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 7.9×.

Shareholder yield of 2.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
